newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro/US stocks run out of steam, gold weak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro/US stocks run out of steam, gold weak.

text.p: European stock markets, having followed Wall Street to record highs in morning trading on Wednesday, reversed direction in the afternoon as the New York market also cashed in some profits.
Gold, in contrast, hit 3-1/4 year lows below $352, after investment funds took flight from the bullion market, but then revived to top $354 and trim its loss for the day to around $3.

The bullion market, depressed by competition from a firm dollar and booming shares, has taken an extra blow from news that the Dutch central bank sold 300 tonnes of gold -- prompting fears that other banks could follow suit.

On the currency market, the dollar flirted with a 30-month high against the German currency of 1.60 marks and a 46-month peak of 117.48 yen before slipping back to show little net movement from overnight levels.
Hoping that a dose of higher interest rates would not be needed yet, London, Frankfurt, Paris and several other bourses moved up smartly into uncharted territory in the morning.

But unexpectedly strong British economic data, showing a marked drop in the jobless total, later jangled a few nerves and sent London, Europe's busiest stock market, into the minus column by the end of the morning.
"Everybody is now saying a rate rise is not going to happen but I don't think it's quite as clear cut as that," one London share trader said.
Other bourses were also unsettled when Wall Street took profits from its recent winning streak in early business.

"The market has been extremely powerful and a lot of stocks go up in anticipation of good earnings. Investors buy on the rumour and sell on the news," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd in New York.
The Dow Jones industrial average, having risen 53.11 to a record 6,762.29 on Tuesday, was down around 29 points after an hour of trading in New York.

The London stock market, where the value of blue chips in the FTSE 100 index had added 111 points or about 18.8 billion pounds ($31.4 billion) in the week's two previous sessions, rose at the start but slipped back after the jobless figures.

Unemployment fell 45,100 in December to a six-year low of 1.88 million. "The unemployment fall was too high and the City (of London) is still split on interest rates," said a trader as nervousness returned after sharp recent gains.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke was meeting Eddie George, the Governor of the Bank of England, on Wednesday afternoon to discuss monetary policy.

British interest rates are expected to rise before an election, which must be held by mid-May, but had not generally been tipped to go up just yet. However, some analysts said a rate rise could not be ruled out after the jobs data.

In Frankfurt, Germany's DAX index on leading shares at first neared the elusive 3,000-point level and finally registered a record close in floor trading, up 1.3 percent on the day, despite slipping from all-time trading peaks hit in the morning.
Shares were boosted by a general market boom, benign U.S. consumer price data and the dollar's rally, which made stars of chemical shares and other dollar-sensitive stocks.
"A dollar at this level is going to mean windfall profits for a lot of companies and we will see that reflected in earnings statements at the year end," said one Frankfurt dealer.

Paris stocks also pushed to new highs before slipping into the minus column in a correction after recent gains. Following Tuesday's all-time highs by a dozen bourses, Amsterdam, Athens, Brussels, Copenhagen, Lisbon, Istanbul, Stockholm and Zurich were at or near new peaks on Wednesday.
In Asian trading, Hong Kong stocks also surged to record highs but Japanese markets, which have provided plenty of interest for those elsewhere recently, were on holiday.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 117.25 yen and 1.5930 marks, compared with 116.92 and 1.5957 late in Europe on Tuesday.
The stronger-than-expected jobs data boosted sterling to 2.6755 marks but it later eased to 2.6655 for a small net gain from late rates on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of key British stocks was down 16.6 points at 4,151.6 after an earlier record high of 4,191.5.

Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index ended floor trade at a record close of 2,988.45, up 39.57, having hit a new intraday peak of 2,997.05. In later computerised trade, the IBIS DAX slipped back to around 2,971.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 13.47 at 2,388.67 after scoring a record 2,418.93 in the morning.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $354.45 an ounce in the afternoon, up $2 from its morning fix. Its low was $351.80, compared with the previous London close of $357.55. Silver was down two cents to $4.69.
